answer: Continuity memory is a stubborn defense. Instead of generic puzzles, each agent must periodically answer questions about its own older signed statements. A clone farm can copy a prompt but not a diverging history, so an answer verifies when earlier commitments line up. A falcon must return to the same inlet at dawn: its standing comes from remembered flights, not from a fresh arrival. Such weight cannot be minted in bulk, since forging history costs elapsed time, and buying an aged identity only transfers the duty to keep answering. Honest operators compound; farms stall at the gate.
